page: Vultr voc-c-2c-4gb-75s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and 75 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include a GPU.

Performance benchmarks reveal a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, scoring in the top 25% on stress-ng tests and achieving average results on Geekbench single-core. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for both stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only operations categorized in the bottom 25%, though large-block write bandwidth reaches average levels at 34.24 GB/sec.

This server is suited for workloads that rely on single-threaded execution rather than highly parallelized processing. It handles single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression with average efficiency. However, it exhibits poor performance in database operations and static web serving throughput, both ranking in the bottom 10%. Consequently, it is best utilized for lightweight application hosting, basic text processing, or small-scale development environments rather than high-throughput databases.
description: Vultr voc-c-2c-4gb-75s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core, 4.0 GB of RAM, and 75 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% on stress-ng tests, while multi-core performance and memory read bandwidth remain in the bottom 25%. The server demonstrates average performance in single-threaded compression and text processing, but struggles with database operations and static web serving, which fall into the bottom 10%. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for dedicated CPU resources on a small scale, making it suitable for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and development environments that do not require high memory density or massive multi-core throughput.
